Tzolkin: The Mayan Calendar presents a new game mechanism: dynamic worker placement. Players representing different Mayan tribes place their workers on giant connected gears, and as the gears rotate they take the workers to different action spots. During a turn, players can either (a) place one or more workers on the lowest visible spot of the gears or (b) pick up one or more workers. When placing workers, they must pay corn, which is used as a currency in the game. When they pick up a worker, they perform certain actions depending on the position of the worker. Actions located "later" on the gears are more valuable, so it's wise to let the time work for you – but players cannot skip their turn; if they have all their workers on the gears, they have to pick some up. The game ends after one full revolution of the central Tzolkin gear. There are many paths to victory. Pleasing the gods by placing crystal skulls in deep caves or building many temples are just two of those many paths... Number of players: 2 - 4 Game duration: 30 mn Complexity: 4 / 5 Play Tzolk'in and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. (Turn in all corn, take 3 corn and move one step down on any temple) - Either place workers OR pick up workers -- Placing workers : pay corn for the number of workers you place. The cost for the number of workers you place is 0, 1, 3, 6, 10, or 15 for, respectively, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 workers placed on that turn, plus the cumulative cost noted next to each of your placed workers. --- Starting Player Space : When you take this non-gear action, three things happen: You'll get the food that has accumulated on the T'zolkin gear teeth You get the worker back at the end of the round You either become start player, or pass start player to your left -- Picking up Workers : You may pick up one or more of your placed workers. For each worker picked up either --- Use the action where your worker was standing --- Use a lower action on the wheel from where your worker was standing(if not standing on a free action space,pay 1 corn for each step back) --- Do nothing. Food Day Players must feed their workers at the end of Day 8, Day 14, Day 21, and Day 27. - Feed the Workers Each players must pay 2 corn for each worker they have in play (on a gear or in front of you) with the exception for any farms you own. You must feed as many workers as you have corn for. -- For each worker not fed, you lose 3 points - Take Rewards -- Middle of Age (Brown days) --- Receive items shown on the left edge of temples from step you are on and all steps below -- End of Age (Teal Days) --- Remove all Age 1 buildings and fill spaces with Age 2 buildings --- Receive points shown on the right edge of temples for the step you are on. --- Bonus points on each temple track for the player whose marker is highest. Bonus amount is shown above each temple. For ties, everyone receives half the bonus. Advance the Calendar If there is no worker on the starting player space, place a corn on the current Tzolk'in gear tooth and advance the gear one day. [Rating: 1/10] I came here, because of all the people rating mature themed games like KD:M or Hate with a 1, just because of their mature theme. This games theme is boring!

[Rating: 1/10] Another Tascini horror - painfully overconvoluted puzzles perambulating in pointless patterns on a pretty plan to no particular purpose. Too much work,  not enough game.

[Rating: 1/10] There's a few cute ideas here, like tokens investing time to get better rewards. It's not all bad!

[Rating: 1/10] The gear wheel is a brilliant mechanic that I wish it wasn't stuck in a game that suffers so much from a dominant strategy issue, every game plays so samey with someone going corn, someone going resources + building, another going all in on skulls etc. Maybe the expansion fixes that but I really don't care enough to find out.

[Rating: 1.5/10] The game itself is an inventive worker placement game so let's say a 6.5.   Theme is -5 for getting Maya civilization and culture so incredibly wrong. There's not even an actual Tzolk'in in the game at all and it's clear the designers not only knew nothing about the subject matter, but didn't even bother to do cursory research on Wikipedia. I've read a couple articles about what this game gets wrong and they don't even get into the worst of it, honestly.   I really expected this game would at least include the Mesoamerican 260 day calendar considering of 13 numbers and 20 day signs as part of 

[Rating: 2/10] This game has standard to sub-standard mechanics. The novelty gear, is for me the only innovative thing this game has going for it. But it gets old quickly, very quickly. It's just basically a convenient way to make a standing worker gather more/better resources. But watching workers revolve on a piece of gear and wait for them to reach their stop is as exciting as watching paint dry. The theme is pasted on and I was bored after 15 minutes. No thanks.

[Rating: 2/10] I hate this game.  Too many shortcomings in gameplay meant only to justify that silly wheel mechanic. Massive and unmitigated first-player advantage to start the game.  Dont play this game with 5 players (w/expansion) because it just gets worse.

[Rating: 2/10] A hot mess of mechanisms, combinations, rules and choices. Makes my brain shut down. Much too complex for my taste. Reminds me of Hawaii and many other games with too many choices and ways to score. It's a puzzle, not a game. Has zero fun factor. Would rate it a 1 if not for the unique gear mechanism. Never need to play it again.

[Rating: 2/10] I don't get the hype. The gears are neat but seems to be on the only thing that stands out in the game. It maybe a bit harsh to call them a gimmick but they aren't too far off. The game is dry and oh so boring. The first player seems to have a big advantage. The first time I played it I didn't take enough corn and I was boned for the rest of the game. At the end one of the players was like "Oh yeah, that is the wrong opening move" but didn't have any other move because I was last player. I don't mind euros but this is the worst type of euro. [Rating: 2/10] Seems very random and chaotic to me.  I am not good at thinking more than a couple of moves in advance so this game was overwhelming.  I hope to never play it again.  On Board Game Arena
